question: What are the candidate therapeutic targets, immune pathways and biomarkers in ulcerative colitis with the strongest convergent evidence?

models.orchestrator: Claude Opus 5.5 — Claude Code main session
models.agents: Claude Sonnet 5.5 — Claude Code subagents (agente-expresion, agente-literatura, agente-externo, agente-celular, agente-vias, agente-aplicado)

findings.statement: CHI3L1 has the largest consistent increase among the convergence leaders, significant upward in all five cohorts: pooled UC vs control log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.71] with padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.8e-33].

CHI3L1 is already raised in non-inflamed MSCCR mucosa (log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.84]) and rises further in inflamed vs non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient (paired log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.62]), so it tracks both the disease background and local inflammation.

CXCR2, first in the convergence ranking, is up in all five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264], padj [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=2.94e-23]) and higher in inflamed than paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.70]); as a neutrophil receptor its bulk rise may come from infiltrating cells.

CXCR2 is modestly raised already in non-inflamed MSCCR mucosa (log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.64], padj [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=6.23e-8]), much less than in inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=2.60]).

CXCL8 is strictly local to inflamed mucosa: unchanged in non-inflamed MSCCR mucosa (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0037], padj [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.986]) but up in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.97]), the pattern of a marker of active inflammation.

CXCL8 replicates in all five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.70], padj [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.27e-17]), with the largest fold change in the small Leuven infliximab cohort (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=7.21]).

HMGCS2, the ketogenic enzyme of colonocytes, is lost in UC in all five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.58]) but is normal in non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.065], padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.675]) and falls in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.95]): loss of epithelial metabolism follows local inflammation.

CLDN8 is the strongest decrease (meta log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.52], padj [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=1.86e-25]) and, unlike HMGCS2, is already lost from non-inflamed mucosa (non-inflamed vs control log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-1.60], padj [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=9.66e-14]), a barrier change present beyond the inflamed segment.

The colonocyte water channel AQP8 is strongly reduced, significant downward in four of five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.31], padj [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=2.34e-19]); like PCK1, UGT2A3 and SLC26A2 it marks loss of differentiated epithelium, a biomarker rather than a target.

DUOX2 rises in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.48]); non-inflamed mucosa already shows a smaller rise (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.81]); the meta-analysis is significant in all five cohorts (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.32]).

SERPINB5 has the most significant meta-analysis result of the top ranking (padj [gene=SERPINB5; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.81e-135]); non-inflamed mucosa already shows a rise (log2FC [gene=SERPINB5; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.04]).

REG1A does not replicate in every cohort: it is up in four cohorts but not significant in the Leuven infliximab cohort despite a large fold change there (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]), so its replication is four of five.

OSMR is up in all five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.04]) and in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.88]), with only a small change in non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.18]).

The ligand OSM is up in all five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=OSM; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.88], padj [gene=OSM; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=9.45e-9]) with high heterogeneity between cohorts (I2 [gene=OSM; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; i2=0.941]).

CCL2 is up in the meta-analysis (log2FC [gene=CCL2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.28]) but only four cohorts have data, and its paired inflamed vs non-inflamed change is small (log2FC [gene=CCL2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.74]).

IDO1 is up in all five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.45], padj [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=1.05e-15]) and in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.68]).

TNF, an approved UC target and positive control, changes only modestly in biopsies and is significant in four cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=TNF; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.74], padj [gene=TNF; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.95e-14]): a validated target need not be among the largest transcript changes.

ITGB7, the vedolizumab target, barely changes and is significant in only three cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=ITGB7; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.41], padj [gene=ITGB7; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=0.0381]), so expression alone would miss this approved target.

SLC6A14 has the largest pooled increase (log2FC [gene=SLC6A14; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=5.02]) but data in only four cohorts and very high heterogeneity (I2 [gene=SLC6A14; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; i2=0.982]), so its size is uncertain.

Literature supports CHI3L1 as up in UC and correlated with NLRP3 inflammasome expression, and one study reports that it promotes macrophage pyroptosis via BCAT1/NF-kappaB, with CHI3L1 inhibition protective; this is a single mechanistic study, not clinical targeting.
The only CHI3L1-directed compound in the corpus is velpatasvir, which binds recombinant CHI3L1 with micromolar affinity in a repurposing study; there is no clinical-stage CHI3L1 agent.

Literature describes the axis of CXCL8 with CXCR1 and CXCR2 as participating in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling, and CXCL8 appears as a blood diagnostic marker for IBD, but these are review and bioinformatic statements, not trials.

One study reports IDO1 elevated in UC and driving M1 macrophage polarisation via ER stress (GRP78-XBP1); an IDO inhibitor (methyl-tryptophan) ameliorated DSS colitis in mice. Support is preclinical and from a single paper.

DUOX2 is among the most elevated proteins in inflamed UC biopsies vs healthy controls in a proteomic study and is shared by IBD and colorectal cancer; a herbal formula (TLXDS) was reported to act by inhibiting DUOX2 overexpression.
Calprotectin transcripts (S100A8/S100A9) are associated with endoscopic disease and S100A8 is proposed as a diagnostic biomarker of UC, consistent with the established faecal calprotectin test.
Literature agrees that HMGCS2 (with AQP8) is decreased in UC and reports a high diagnostic value; it is a biomarker of epithelial injury, not a target.

MMP1 support in the corpus is bioinformatic: a diagnostic signature, a correlation with macrophage infiltration and a docking prediction of ilomastat as an inhibitor; there is no experimental UC targeting.
CXCL1 appears in the literature as overexpressed in pancolitis and as part of machine-learning diagnostic gene sets, i.e. biomarker rather than target support.

Despite ranking first, CXCR2 has no verbatim-validated UC literature relation in the corpus; its literature support is only the Open Targets literature score ([gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; literature=0.7203]), so published UC evidence for CXCR2 blockade is thin here.

OSMR likewise has no extracted UC literature relation and a low Open Targets literature score ([gene=OSMR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; literature=0.1311]), although its genetic association score is [gene=OSMR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.6089].

JAK2 is the second Open Targets UC target (association [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318], genetic association [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8458]), a positive control for the JAK-inhibitor class, yet its biopsy change is small (meta log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.87]).

IL12B (ustekinumab target) heads the Open Targets UC list (association [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7424]) and is a positive control for approved UC biology.
TNF has an Open Targets UC association of [gene=TNF; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6336] and approved anti-TNF biologics; it is a positive control.

S1PR1, target of approved S1P modulators, has an Open Targets association of [gene=S1PR1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5937] and is up in all five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=S1PR1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.20]), an approved target that also changes in biopsies.

CXCR2 has strong genetic support (Open Targets genetic association [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8171]) and clinical antagonists (reparixin up to phase 3; navarixin, ladarixin and SX-682 in phase 2), none approved for UC.
STRING places CXCR2 at the hub of the ELR+ chemokines, with near-maximal confidence partners CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCL5 and CXCL2, several of which are themselves in the top convergence list.

FCGR2A has the highest genetic association of the top 25 ([gene=FCGR2A; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.87]; overall [gene=FCGR2A; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5543]) but no drug and only a modest paired inflamed change (log2FC [gene=FCGR2A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.48]).

OSMR is antibody-tractable with an advanced clinical antibody (vixarelimab, phase 2) and belongs to the Reactome IL-6-type cytokine receptor pathway; it is the most druggable stromal receptor among the leaders.

CHI3L1 has no human genetic support and a low Open Targets UC association ([gene=CHI3L1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.1136]) and no clinical drug, but predicted antibody and small-molecule tractability (high-quality pocket, structure with ligand).

UniProt describes CHI3L1 as a secreted lectin without chitinase activity that mediates AKT1 activation and IL8 production in colonic epithelial cells and facilitates invasion of enteric bacteria into colonic mucosa.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in five cohorts with genetic association [gene=CD274; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.5911], but its drugs (atezolizumab, sugemalimab) block PD-L1 and would act in the wrong direction for colitis; it is a marker of interferon-driven inflammation, not a UC drug target.
IL1B has approved blockade (canakinumab) but no genetic association with UC in Open Targets ([gene=IL1B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0]).

IDO1 is tractable with clinical inhibitors (epacadostat, linrodostat) but lacks genetic support ([gene=IDO1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0]); IDO inhibition is immune-activating, so its direction for colitis is uncertain.
CCL2 combines genetic support ([gene=CCL2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.5829]) with a phase 2 antibody (carlumab).

IL2RA has genetic support ([gene=IL2RA; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.6619]) and approved antibodies (basiliximab), and is up in five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=IL2RA; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.50]).

MMP9 has a phase 3 antibody (andecaliximab) and broad MMP inhibitors but no genetic association ([gene=MMP9; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0]); the stromal MMPs that lead on expression (MMP1, MMP3) have only broad-spectrum inhibitors.

In Gubatan inflamed mucosa nearly all CXCR2 transcripts are neutrophil (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]); in Smillie, which lacks neutrophils, the lineage call (T/NK) does not replicate in the second dataset. After composition adjustment only a small part of the bulk increase remains (adjusted log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.44], retained [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]): the CXCR2 signal is mostly neutrophil influx.

CXCL8 loses significance after composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.32], padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0527]; verdict composition) and is mostly made by neutrophils (share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]), so its bulk rise reflects neutrophil influx; the adjustment can over-correct, so this is not proof of pure influx.

CXCR1 is a neutrophil gene (share [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]) whose bulk increase is largely composition (retained [gene=CXCR1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.195]).

AQP9 is made by neutrophils (share [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]) and retains only part of its increase after adjustment (retained [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.261]): a neutrophil-influx marker.

S100A8 is neutrophil-derived (share [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]) and keeps a smaller but significant change after adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.92], retained [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.288]), consistent with its use as an inflammation biomarker.
S100A9 is likewise mostly neutrophil (share [gene=S100A9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.887]).

OSM transcripts in inflamed mucosa come mostly from neutrophils (share [gene=OSM; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]), so the ligand side of the OSM axis is carried by infiltrating neutrophils.

OSMR is stromal (lineage share [gene=OSMR; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.907], replicated in the second dataset), led by inflammatory fibroblasts, with a low neutrophil share ([gene=OSMR; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.078]); its bulk change is partly composition (retained [gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.222], adjusted padj [gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=8.26e-6]), plausibly because activated stroma raises the stromal score itself.

CHI3L1 is made by inflammatory fibroblasts in Smillie (share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.652]; stromal lineage replicated), with a neutrophil contribution in Gubatan (share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.466]), and keeps a significant change after adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.40], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=1.63e-16]): a tissue change, not only influx.

MMP1 comes from inflammatory fibroblasts (Smillie share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.531], stromal lineage replicated; Gubatan share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed_with_neutrophils.0.share=0.681]) and keeps a significant adjusted change (log2FC [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.26], padj [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=2.36e-15]).

DUOX2 is epithelial (lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], replicated), expressed by most inflamed enterocytes ([gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.pct_expressing=77.7%] of cells) but few in health, with negligible neutrophil share, and keeps a significant adjusted change (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.32], padj [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=1.83e-9]): an intrinsic epithelial response.

IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie (lineage share [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.598], replicated), but in Gubatan enterocytes make the largest share ([gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed_with_neutrophils.0.share=0.427]); its adjusted change remains significant (log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.85]).

CD274 is largely neutrophil in Gubatan (share [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]) and partly composition (retained [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.384]).

The genetically supported FCGR2A is mostly expressed by neutrophils in inflamed mucosa (share [gene=FCGR2A; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.861]), so its bulk rise is likely neutrophil-driven.
IL1B transcripts in inflamed mucosa are mainly neutrophil (share [gene=IL1B; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.702]).

LCN2, often read as a neutrophil marker, is made almost entirely by non-neutrophil cells in inflamed UC mucosa (neutrophil share [gene=LCN2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.043]), i.e. an epithelial antimicrobial response.

SERPINB5 has a low neutrophil share ([gene=SERPINB5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.05]), so its strong, replicated increase is a tissue change rather than influx.

TNFa pathway activity is up in all five cohorts (t in UNIFI [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]); it is the axis of approved anti-TNF biologics, a positive control.
NFkB pathway activity is up in all five cohorts (t in UNIFI [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=18.79]), running in parallel with TNFa.
JAK-STAT activity is up in all five cohorts (t in MSCCR [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]), the axis targeted by approved JAK inhibitors.

TGFb activity is up in all five cohorts with the largest t in UNIFI ([type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=25.17]); no UC drug targets it, and it reflects stromal activation and repair as much as inflammation.

EGFR, MAPK, hypoxia, PI3K and VEGF activities are also up in all five cohorts (EGFR t in MSCCR [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=18.08]), so broad pathway activation does not discriminate between mechanisms.

Not every pathway is robust: p53 is lower in only three cohorts (Leuven infliximab t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE16879.t=-3.59]), WNT is not significant in GSE73661 (padj [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE73661.padj=0.0637]) and Androgen is mixed (up in one cohort, down in two).
STAT3 inferred activity is up in all five cohorts (t in UNIFI [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0]), the shared node of IL-6/gp130, OSM and JAK signalling.

NFKB1 and AP1 activities are up in all five cohorts (NFKB1 t in MSCCR [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=19.75]; AP1 t in UNIFI [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=19.49]), convergent inflammatory transcription rather than a single circuit.

The epithelial TF HNF4A is not consistently changed despite the loss of epithelial metabolism genes: down in PURSUIT (t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE92415.t=-4.61]) but up in GSE73661 (t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE73661.t=2.61]).

The most specific neutrophil circuit is CXCL8 from Neutrophil CXCR4 to Neutrophil via CXCR2, stronger in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]): an autocrine/paracrine neutrophil recruitment loop addressed by clinical CXCR2 antagonists but not by approved UC drugs. Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

The neutrophil-to-fibroblast OSM circuit is weak: Neutrophil OSM to LP fibroblast via IL6ST scores lower in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]); only a Neutrophil PADI4 to LP fibroblast pair appears de novo from a zero baseline.

IL1B from monocyte-derived macrophages pairs with the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophil states (to Neutrophil PADI4, log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.168]), which may reflect IL-1 buffering rather than signalling.

Higher baseline TNFa pathway activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.t_nr_vs_r=4.79], BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]), infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]), vedolizumab and golimumab, but also with placebo non-response in UNIFI (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]): it marks severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism.

JAK-STAT activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) and infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.0284]), not vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]); the UNIFI placebo arm is borderline (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0543]).

TGFb activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) and infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.0136]) but also with UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]).

Baseline OSM is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (difference [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.diff_nr_minus_r=0.651], BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) and not significantly in the UNIFI placebo arm (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), but the drug-by-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.971]) and the golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms do not survive correction: no evidence of a drug-specific OSM effect.

TREM1 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) and also with UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), so it marks severity.

CXCR2 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]), with no interaction (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]): neutrophil burden marks severe disease regardless of drug.

CHI3L1 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.00971]) and even more so in UNIFI placebo non-responders (difference [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.575], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0203]): a severity marker, not a marker of drug-specific failure.

Baseline ITGB7, the vedolizumab target, is not associated with vedolizumab response (difference [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.diff_nr_minus_r=-0.011], BH padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]).

Baseline IL23A is not associated with ustekinumab response (BH padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]): target expression does not stratify response to the drug that blocks it.

SDR16C5 is the strongest first-in-class candidate with an intrinsic change: up in five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.55]), retaining most of its increase after composition adjustment (retained [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.66]), epithelial (lineage share [gene=SDR16C5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.918], replicated; goblet cells lead in Gubatan), antibody-tractable, with low vital-organ RNA ([gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=26.9] nTPM). Its function in colitis is unknown.

XKR9 has the highest retained share after adjustment ([gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.80], epithelial) but is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=2] cohorts, so it fails the replication standard of the other leaders.

CPXM1 is a stromal candidate (inflammatory fibroblasts lead, share [gene=CPXM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.213]; lineage replicated) up in five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.64]), partly composition (retained [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.41]), with low vital-organ RNA ([gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=9.1] nTPM).

LAX1 tops the discovery list by fold change (meta log2FC [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.79]) but is a T/NK gene that keeps little of its increase after adjustment (retained [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.23]), so it likely reflects lymphocyte influx.

ADGRG3 passes the discovery filters and is tractable by antibody and small molecule, but its transcripts are neutrophil (share [gene=ADGRG3; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; neutrophil_share=0.906]), so it is a neutrophil target, not a tissue one.

PCDH17 retains almost none of its increase after composition adjustment (retained [gene=PCDH17; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.098]), the weakest tissue-intrinsic evidence among the discovery hits.

CHRDL2, a stromal discovery hit, has the highest vital-organ RNA among the leading discovery candidates ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM), a safety point to check.

caveats: Single-agent run: all six specialist roles were done by one agent with fewer tool calls per stream than the multi-agent design.
Microarray fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq; compare directions and significance across cohorts, not sizes.
Composition adjustment can over-correct because lineage scores rise when resident cells activate; losing significance after adjustment is not proof of pure influx.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression, not proof of signalling.
Treatment associations are baseline associations with response, not predictions; small arms (infliximab, vedolizumab, PURSUIT placebo) have little power.
The literature corpus is a few hundred UC abstracts; absence of relations is not absence of literature.

summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in ulcerative colitis mucosa is the neutrophil-recruitment axis of CXCR2, CXCR1 and their ligand CXCL8. CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking: it is raised in all five biopsy cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264]), local to inflamed mucosa, genetically supported in Open Targets and has clinical-stage antagonists, none approved in UC. Single-cell data place almost all CXCR2 transcripts in neutrophils and composition adjustment removes most of its bulk change, so the axis reads first as a marker of neutrophil influx and only secondarily as a target on recruited neutrophils.

The candidates that hold up best as tissue-level targets are those whose increase survives composition adjustment in a replicated cell of origin: CHI3L1 and MMP1 in inflammatory fibroblasts, DUOX2 in enterocytes and IDO1 in myeloid cells and epithelium. OSMR, the stromal oncostatin M receptor, is the only leader that combines genetic support with a clinical antibody (vixarelimab), but most of its bulk rise tracks composition. CHI3L1 is the most consistent expression change and is tractable but has no genetic support and no drug.

The most reproducible biomarkers are the loss of epithelial metabolic and barrier genes (CLDN8, HMGCS2, AQP8), down in all or nearly all cohorts, and the gain of neutrophil and antimicrobial genes (S100A8, AQP9, CXCL8, DUOX2, LCN2). Some changes are local to inflamed mucosa (CXCL8, HMGCS2), whereas others are already present in non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients (CLDN8, CHI3L1, SERPINB5) and may mark the disease state itself.

TNFa, NFkB and JAK-STAT pathway activity and STAT3 transcription-factor activity are raised in all five cohorts; these axes are already targeted by approved UC drugs and act as positive controls, as do IL12B, JAK2, TNF and S1PR1 in Open Targets. In the trial cohorts, baseline TNFa activity, CXCR2, TREM1, CHI3L1 and OSM are higher in ustekinumab non-responders but also in placebo non-responders or without a drug-by-placebo interaction, so they mark severity rather than drug-specific resistance; baseline IL23A and ITGB7 do not stratify response to the drugs that block them.

As first-in-class hypotheses, the discovery screen proposes SDR16C5, an epithelial (goblet and transit-amplifying cell) gene whose increase is largely intrinsic and replicated in five cohorts, and CPXM1, an inflammatory-fibroblast gene; both are antibody-tractable with low vital-organ expression but lack functional data in colitis.

expression.text: The random-effects meta-analysis across the five cohorts identifies a large, reproducible inflammatory program. The strongest consistent increase among the convergence leaders is CHI3L1 (pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.71], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.8e-33]), significant upward in every cohort.

Alongside CHI3L1, the up-regulated program is dominated by neutrophil chemokines and receptors (CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCR2, CXCR1), calprotectin (S100A8, S100A9), antimicrobial and oxidative epithelial genes (DUOX2, DUOXA2, LCN2, REG1A) and stromal metalloproteinases (MMP1, MMP3, MMP7), together with IDO1 and SERPINB5. SLC6A14 has the largest pooled increase of all (log2FC [gene=SLC6A14; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=5.02]) but is measured in four cohorts with very high heterogeneity (I2 [gene=SLC6A14; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; i2=0.982]), so its size is uncertain. Approved UC targets change little in comparison: TNF (meta log2FC [gene=TNF; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.74]) and ITGB7 (meta log2FC [gene=ITGB7; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.41]), so the size of a transcript change is not a measure of therapeutic value.

The decreased genes describe loss of differentiated colonocyte function: the tight-junction gene CLDN8 is the strongest decrease (meta log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.52]), followed by the water channel AQP8 (meta log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.31]), the gluconeogenic PCK1, the glucuronidase UGT2A3, the ketogenic enzyme HMGCS2 (meta log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.58]) and the sulfate transporter SLC26A2. These are robust biomarkers of epithelial injury and metabolic failure rather than drug targets.

inflammation.text: Comparing inflamed and non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients separates local from background changes. CXCL8 is a pure marker of local inflammation: the non-inflamed vs control contrast is flat (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0037], padj [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.986]) while the paired inflamed vs non-inflamed contrast is strongly positive (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.97]).

HMGCS2 shows the same local pattern on the down side: normal in non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.065], padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.675]) and falling in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.95]), so epithelial metabolic loss follows local inflammation.

CLDN8, by contrast, is already lost from non-inflamed mucosa (non-inflamed vs control log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-1.60], padj [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=9.66e-14]), a barrier change present beyond the inflamed segment that may mark the disease state itself.

CHI3L1 combines both patterns: the non-inflamed vs control contrast is already positive (log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.84]) and the paired inflamed vs non-inflamed contrast adds a further rise (log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.62]).

DUOX2 behaves similarly: a rise in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.48]), with non-inflamed mucosa already showing a smaller rise (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.81]).

SERPINB5 has the most significant meta-analysis result among the leaders (padj [gene=SERPINB5; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.81e-135]); non-inflamed mucosa already shows a rise (log2FC [gene=SERPINB5; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.04]), and its low neutrophil share ([gene=SERPINB5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.05]) makes it a tissue change.

OSMR is mainly a local change: a rise in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.88]) with only a small non-inflamed vs control shift (log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.18]). The paired increase of IDO1 (log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.68]) is also local.

replication.text: The discovery cohort's leading changes reproduce well in the four microarray cohorts: every leading convergence gene except CCL2 changes in the same direction in all five cohorts. CXCL8, for example, replicates everywhere (meta padj [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.27e-17]) and is largest in the small Leuven infliximab cohort (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=7.21]), a reminder that array fold changes are compressed and cohort sizes differ, so directions and significance are compared, not magnitudes.

REG1A is the clearest partial replication: up in four cohorts but not significant in the Leuven infliximab cohort despite a large fold change there (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]).

CCL2 has data in only four cohorts and a modest paired inflamed vs non-inflamed rise (log2FC [gene=CCL2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.74]), so its convergence rests on genetics and a phase 2 antibody more than on expression.

literature.text: Literature support in the corpus is mostly biomarker-level and mechanistic. Calprotectin transcripts (S100A8 with S100A9) are associated with endoscopic disease and proposed as diagnostic markers, HMGCS2 is reported decreased in UC with diagnostic value, and CXCL1 and MMP1 appear in bioinformatic diagnostic signatures; DUOX2 is among the most elevated proteins in inflamed UC biopsies in a proteomic study. Mechanistic single studies report that CHI3L1 promotes macrophage pyroptosis via BCAT1/NF-kappaB and that IDO1 drives M1 macrophage polarisation, with an IDO inhibitor protective in mouse colitis; the axis of CXCL8 with CXCR1 and CXCR2 is described as participating in UC pathogenesis. None of these is a clinical trial.

The literature is silent where other streams are strongest. CXCR2, first in the ranking, has no verbatim-validated UC literature relation in the corpus and rests only on the Open Targets literature score ([gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; literature=0.7203]); published UC evidence for CXCR2 blockade is thin here.

OSMR likewise has no extracted UC relation and a low Open Targets literature score ([gene=OSMR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; literature=0.1311]) despite genetic support.

The only CHI3L1-directed compound in the corpus is velpatasvir, which binds recombinant CHI3L1 with micromolar affinity in a repurposing study, so CHI3L1 has mechanistic but not pharmacological validation.

external.text: Approved UC targets appear as positive controls in Open Targets: IL12B heads the list (association [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7424]), with JAK2, TNF and S1PR1 also near the top. JAK2 has strong genetic support (genetic association [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8458]) yet a small biopsy change (meta log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.87]), and S1PR1 is one of the few approved targets that also rises clearly in biopsies (meta log2FC [gene=S1PR1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.20]).

Among expression-led leaders, genetics supports CXCR2 (genetic association [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8171]), FCGR2A ([gene=FCGR2A; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.87]), IL2RA, OSMR, CCL2 and CD274. CXCR2 has clinical antagonists (reparixin up to phase 3, navarixin, ladarixin and SX-682 in phase 2), OSMR an antibody-tractable profile with vixarelimab in phase 2, CCL2 the antibody carlumab and IL2RA approved antibodies such as basiliximab, none approved in UC. FCGR2A has no drug. CD274 drugs block PD-L1, the wrong direction for colitis, so CD274 is a marker of interferon-driven inflammation, not a target.

The strongest expression changes mostly lack genetic support. CHI3L1 has a low Open Targets association ([gene=CHI3L1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.1136]) and no drug, but predicted antibody and small-molecule tractability; UniProt describes it as a secreted lectin that drives AKT1 activation and IL8 production in colonic epithelial cells.

IL1B (canakinumab), IDO1 (epacadostat, linrodostat) and MMP9 (andecaliximab) have clinical drugs from other indications but no genetic association with UC; IDO inhibition is immune-activating, so its direction for colitis is uncertain, and the stromal MMPs that lead on expression have only broad-spectrum inhibitors. STRING places CXCR2 at the hub of the ELR+ chemokines CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCL5 and CXCL2, which are themselves among the leaders.

cells.text: Single-cell data separate tissue targets from markers of cell influx. In the Gubatan dataset, which captures neutrophils, CXCR2 transcripts are almost entirely neutrophil (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]); in Smillie, which lacks neutrophils, the residual lineage call does not replicate. After composition adjustment CXCR2 keeps only a small part of its bulk increase (retained [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]).

CXCL8 is mostly neutrophil (share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]) and loses significance after adjustment (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0527]), the only leader with a full composition verdict. CXCR1, AQP9, S100A8, S100A9, OSM, IL1B, FCGR2A and CD274 are also neutrophil-dominated, so their bulk rises largely reflect neutrophil influx. Because lineage scores rise when resident cells activate, the adjustment can over-correct: losing significance is not proof of pure influx.

CHI3L1 is made by inflammatory fibroblasts (Smillie share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.652], stromal lineage replicated), with a neutrophil contribution in Gubatan, and keeps a significant change after adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.40], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=1.63e-16]): a tissue change of activated stroma, not only influx.

DUOX2 is epithelial (lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], replicated), expressed by most inflamed enterocytes ([gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.pct_expressing=77.7%] of cells), and keeps a significant adjusted change (padj [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=1.83e-9]): an intrinsic epithelial response.

MMP1 comes from inflammatory fibroblasts (Gubatan share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed_with_neutrophils.0.share=0.681]) and keeps a significant adjusted change (adjusted log2FC [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.26]).

OSMR is stromal (lineage share [gene=OSMR; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.907], replicated), led by inflammatory fibroblasts, but retains only part of its bulk change after adjustment (retained [gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.222]), which may reflect over-correction of activated stroma.

IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie (lineage share [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.598], replicated) while enterocytes make the largest share in Gubatan, and it keeps a significant adjusted change (adjusted log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.85]).

LCN2, often read as a neutrophil marker, is made almost entirely by non-neutrophil cells (neutrophil share [gene=LCN2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.043]), i.e. an epithelial antimicrobial response.

pathways.text: TNFa, NFkB and JAK-STAT pathway activity is raised in all five cohorts (TNFa t in UNIFI [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]; JAK-STAT t in MSCCR [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]), together with STAT3 ([type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0] in UNIFI), NFKB1 and AP1 transcription-factor activity. These axes are already targeted by approved UC drugs (anti-TNF, JAK inhibitors) and act as positive controls; STAT3 is also the shared node of IL-6/gp130 and OSM signalling.

Untargeted pathways are equally active: TGFb has the largest t in UNIFI ([type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=25.17]) and EGFR, MAPK, hypoxia, PI3K and VEGF are up in all five cohorts, so broad activation does not discriminate mechanisms. Not every pathway is robust: p53 is lower in only three cohorts (Leuven infliximab t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE16879.t=-3.59]), WNT is not significant in GSE73661 (padj [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE73661.padj=0.0637]) and Androgen is mixed. The epithelial TF HNF4A is inconsistent (PURSUIT t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE92415.t=-4.61]) despite the loss of epithelial metabolism genes.

Among specific circuits, the strongest is CXCL8 from Neutrophil CXCR4 to Neutrophil via CXCR2, stronger in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]): an autocrine/paracrine neutrophil recruitment loop addressed by clinical CXCR2 antagonists but by no approved UC drug. The neutrophil OSM to LP fibroblast circuit via IL6ST is weak, scoring lower in inflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]) with only a Neutrophil PADI4 pair appearing from a zero baseline, and macrophage IL1B pairs mainly with the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophils (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.168]), which may be buffering rather than signalling. Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

treatment.text: Higher baseline TNFa pathway activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]), infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]), vedolizumab and golimumab, but also with placebo non-response in UNIFI (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), so it marks severity. TGFb behaves the same way (UNIFI placebo padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]). JAK-STAT is associated with ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) and infliximab non-response but not vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]), with a borderline placebo arm (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0543]).

Baseline OSM is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) and not significantly in the UNIFI placebo arm (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), but the drug-by-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.971]) and no other drug arm survives correction, so there is no evidence of a drug-specific OSM effect.

CXCR2 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]), with no interaction: neutrophil burden marks severe disease regardless of drug.

TREM1 follows the same severity pattern (ustekinumab BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]; UNIFI placebo padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]).

CHI3L1 separates UNIFI placebo non-responders even more than ustekinumab non-responders (placebo difference [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.575], BH padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0203]), a severity marker rather than a marker of drug-specific failure.

Target expression does not stratify response to the drug that blocks it: baseline ITGB7 is not associated with vedolizumab response (BH padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]).
Likewise, baseline IL23A is not associated with ustekinumab response (BH padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]).

discovery.text: SDR16C5 is the strongest first-in-class hypothesis. It is up in five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.55]), keeps most of its increase after composition adjustment (retained [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.66]), is epithelial (lineage share [gene=SDR16C5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.918], replicated; goblet and transit-amplifying cells lead), antibody-tractable and has low vital-organ RNA ([gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=26.9] nTPM). What is missing: any functional evidence in colitis, a protein-level confirmation and a reason why a retinol dehydrogenase would be accessible to an antibody.

CPXM1 is a stromal hypothesis: inflammatory fibroblasts lead its expression (share [gene=CPXM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.213]; lineage replicated), it is up in five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.64]) and partly composition (retained [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.41]), with low vital-organ RNA ([gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=9.1] nTPM). It would fit the inflammatory-fibroblast program that also makes CHI3L1, MMP1 and OSMR, but its function in the gut is unknown.

XKR9 has the highest retained share after adjustment ([gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.80], epithelial) but is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=2] cohorts, so it fails the replication standard and is not carried forward.

LAX1 tops the discovery list by fold change (meta log2FC [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.79]) but keeps little of its increase after adjustment (retained [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.23]) as a T/NK gene, so it likely reflects lymphocyte influx.

ADGRG3 passes the filters and is tractable by antibody and small molecule, but its transcripts are neutrophil (share [gene=ADGRG3; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; neutrophil_share=0.906]), making it a neutrophil target rather than a tissue one.

PCDH17 retains almost none of its increase after adjustment (retained [gene=PCDH17; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.098]), the weakest tissue-intrinsic evidence among the discovery hits.

CHRDL2, a stromal hit, has the highest vital-organ RNA among the leading discovery candidates ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM), a safety point to check before any development.

integration.text: Expression, replication, genetics and tractability converge most fully on CXCR2 and CXCR1, which are the only leaders with all six evidence streams and clinical antagonists; but the cell stream shows them to be neutrophil genes whose bulk change is mostly influx, and the treatment stream shows CXCR2 to mark severity in placebo arms as well. The second point of convergence is the inflammatory fibroblast: CHI3L1, MMP1, OSMR and the discovery candidate CPXM1 share this cell of origin, keep part of their change after composition adjustment and replicate across cohorts, while TGFb, the pathway most associated with fibroblast activation, is active in every cohort and untargeted.

The streams disagree in three places. Genetics supports JAK2, FCGR2A and CXCR2 but the strongest expression changes (CHI3L1, DUOX2, MMP1, SERPINB5) have no genetic association; approved targets (TNF, ITGB7, IL23A) change little in biopsies and their baseline expression does not stratify response; and the literature corpus is silent on CXCR2 and OSMR, the two leaders with genetic support and drugs, while it describes CHI3L1, IDO1 and DUOX2 mechanistically. The convergence ranking rewards drugs and genetics, so it ranks neutrophil receptors first; weighting cell of origin and composition moves CHI3L1 and the stromal program ahead as tissue targets.

limitations.text: This is the single-agent arm: one agent did the work of six specialists with fewer tool calls per stream, so coverage of genes per stream is narrower than in the multi-agent analysis.

Bulk biopsy transcriptomes mix cell types; the composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells activate, so losing significance after adjustment is not proof of pure influx, and shares in single-cell data compare cell types, not tissue abundance.
Microarray fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq and cohort sizes differ widely; directions and significance are compared across cohorts, not magnitudes.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression and pathway or TF activities are inferred from target genes; neither proves signalling.

Treatment associations are baseline associations with response, not predictions; the infliximab, vedolizumab and PURSUIT placebo arms are small and have little power, and golimumab results did not survive correction for any gene examined.
The literature corpus is a few hundred UC abstracts; absence of a relation is not absence of published work, and drug stages come from Open Targets and do not imply efficacy in UC.

targets.rationale: Ranked first by judgment although eighth numerically: the most consistent increase in all five cohorts, made by replicated inflammatory fibroblasts and keeping a significant change after composition adjustment (a tissue change), tractable by antibody and small molecule, with mechanistic literature on macrophage pyroptosis. Against it: no genetic support, no drug, and it marks severity in placebo arms, so it is also a strong biomarker.

The only leader combining genetic support, a clinical antibody (vixarelimab) and a replicated stromal cell of origin (inflammatory fibroblasts); its ligand OSM is made by neutrophils. Moved up from its numeric rank because it is druggable on resident cells, but its bulk change is partly composition and the neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is weak in single-cell data.

First in the convergence ranking with all six streams: up in five cohorts, local to inflammation, genetic support and clinical antagonists up to phase 3. Moved down because almost all its transcripts are neutrophil and most of its bulk change is influx, so it is a target on recruited neutrophils, not on tissue, and it marks severity in placebo arms.

An intrinsic epithelial change: up in five cohorts, made by inflamed enterocytes in both single-cell datasets and keeping a significant change after adjustment; protein-level literature support. No genetics or drug, so a mechanism of epithelial oxidative stress and a biomarker more than a ready target.

Inflammatory-fibroblast metalloproteinase, up in five cohorts, replicated cell of origin and a significant adjusted change; only broad-spectrum MMP inhibitors exist and literature support is bioinformatic.

Up in five cohorts, myeloid and epithelial origin with a significant adjusted change, clinical inhibitors and mouse data; but no genetic support, and IDO inhibition is immune-activating, so the therapeutic direction is uncertain.

Positive control: second Open Targets UC target with strong genetics and approved JAK-pathway drugs, and JAK-STAT activity is raised in all five cohorts; its own transcript change is small, which is why it ranks lower numerically.

The clearest marker of local inflammation: flat in non-inflamed mucosa, up in inflamed mucosa and in all five cohorts, but mostly neutrophil and fully explained by composition after adjustment, so a biomarker of neutrophil influx rather than a target.
Calprotectin subunit, up in five cohorts, neutrophil-derived and linked in the literature to endoscopic disease: a positive control for biomarker discovery (faecal calprotectin).
Strongest decrease in the meta-analysis and already lost in non-inflamed mucosa, marking barrier injury beyond the inflamed segment; a biomarker, not a target.
Loss of colonocyte ketogenesis in five cohorts, local to inflamed mucosa and supported by the literature as a diagnostic marker: a biomarker of epithelial metabolic failure.

Exploratory: first-in-class epithelial candidate with an intrinsic, five-cohort increase, replicated cell of origin, antibody tractability and low vital-organ expression; no functional data in colitis.
Exploratory: first-in-class inflammatory-fibroblast candidate up in five cohorts with low vital-organ expression, partly composition; function in the gut unknown.
